meta.purpose: Size 13F and 990-PF discovery source classes for scaling the family-office dataset from 24 to 500 qualifying records
meta.goal_context: SFOs are exempt from SEC ADV registration, so the ADV feed cannot find them; 13F (>$100M in 13F securities) and 990-PF (family foundations as leads) are the two candidate net-new channels
meta.every_number_basis: All counts regenerated from live API/file artifacts stored in this census dir; estimates explicitly labeled with basis

apis_used.edgar_fts: https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index (backend of sec.gov/edgar/search) - returns 100 hits/page, aggregations cap at 30 entity buckets, FTS coverage is 2001-present
apis_used.edgar_submissions: https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK##########.json (13F filers carry NO SIC code - cannot auto-classify SFO vs hedge fund)

universe_active_2026.note_QTR3: QTR3 partial as of 2026-07-27; the Q2-2026 holdings wave (period ending 6/30, due 8/14) has not fully landed yet

fts_family_office_all_time.note: EDGAR full-text search, form=13F-HR, phrase 'family office', coverage 2001-2026-07-20
fts_family_office_all_time.interpretation: Phrase match over document text over-captures (includes trust companies/advisers who merely mention family office). Name-contains is the tighter signal.

name_pattern_match_active_2026.tier2_note: Tier-2 is dominated by 'X Family Wealth/Management' RIAs and multi-family offices - wealth managers, not single-family offices

adv_overlap.method: Exact match on normalized names (uppercase, strip punctuation + entity suffixes LLC/LP/INC/etc). ADV uses CRD, 13F uses CIK - no shared key, so name-match is the only join. Undercounts overlap on name variants, so net-new figures are a slight UPPER bound.
adv_overlap.key_finding: Name-matched 'family office'/'family' 13F filers are OVERWHELMINGLY already ADV-registered (multi-family offices register). Only 13 of ~68 name-matched are net-new. The exempt SFOs that ARE net-new mostly do NOT carry 'family' in their name.

neutral_pool_sfo_density_sample.note: Sample also contained foreign banks (BNP Paribas, Banque Transatlantique), insurers (Allstate, Cigna), a sovereign fund (Australia Future Fund), VC/PE GPs, hedge funds, and corporations (United Airlines) - so most of the neutral pool is NOT SFO

knowable_neutral_named_sfos_confirmed_in.validation: Confirmed present in the not-in-ADV pool; submissions API shows they also file SC 13D + Forms 3/4/5 (concentrated holders), consistent with SFO

broad_neutral_pool_extrapolation.estimate: 120-220 SFOs may hide in the 1,688 neutral net-new names (7-13% density x 1688)
broad_neutral_pool_extrapolation.precision: LOW - name gives no signal for neutrally-named SFOs; each requires per-candidate research to distinguish SFO from hedge fund / PE GP / foreign institution / corporation. Submissions API does NOT classify (no SIC on 13F filers).

realistic_qualifying_yield_for_dataset.reasoning: 13-15 high-confidence + a research-limited fraction of the neutral pool. Each neutral candidate needs (1) identification as an SFO not a fund/corp, then (2) affirmative entity establishment (ADR-0020) and a contactable investment decision-maker (ADR-0021). Many neutral candidates will fail verification. Yield is dominated by how much per-candidate research effort is invested.
realistic_qualifying_yield_for_dataset.caveat: 13F only catches SFOs with >$100M in US-listed equities/options; SFOs holding mainly private companies/real estate (e.g. Bezos Expeditions, Walton Enterprises) do NOT appear in the 13F universe at all - confirmed absent from 2026 13F filers

task_b_990pf.framing: 990-PF is a LEAD source, not a countable-entity source. The countable entity for the dataset is a family OFFICE; a family FOUNDATION is a grantmaking vehicle that signals family wealth but is a distinct entity from any associated family office.

national_family_foundation_name_count.method: ProPublica v2 search q='family foundation' summed across 50 states + DC (per-state to bypass the 10,000-result Elasticsearch display cap on the national query)
national_family_foundation_name_count.match_quality: Name-based; top NTEE codes are T22/T20/T21 (private independent/grantmaking/corporate foundations)

sample_characterization.sampling: EINs pulled across spread pages (0,40,...,360) of the national result to span the relevance ranking

family_foundations_over_100m_assets.basis: 29,676 x 2.4% (6/250 sample). CI is wide: 6/250 -> ~0.9-5.2% -> roughly 260-1,540 nationally

leads_to_fo_conversion.countable_entity_gap: A large family foundation is NOT a family office. Conversion requires affirmative evidence of a distinct operating family-office entity associated with the same family.
evidence_that_establishes_the_fo_entity: A distinctly-named family office entity sharing principals/officers with the foundation (e.g. Bezos Expeditions alongside Bezos Family Foundation)
Family office website / press / LinkedIn presence of FO investment staff
An SEC ADV (if registered MFO) or 13F filing by the office entity
Officers/trustees + 'books in care of' listed on the 990-PF itself (starting point for the family, not proof of an FO)
leads_to_fo_conversion.conversion_rate_estimate: 10-25% of >$100M foundation leads convert to a verifiable family-office record
leads_to_fo_conversion.conversion_reasoning: Not every wealthy family with a foundation runs a separate family office; where one exists, affirmatively establishing it (ADR-0020) and finding a contactable investment decision-maker (ADR-0021) filters further. Per-lead research is high-effort.

realistic_qualifying_yield_for_dataset.note: Extending below $100M (>$25M foundations, ~4.8% of 29,676 = ~1,400) widens the lead pool but lowers conversion quality and raises effort per record
realistic_qualifying_yield_for_dataset.illustration: Bezos Family Foundation was in the sample; its associated family office (Bezos Expeditions) does NOT file 13F - the two channels are complementary, and the foundation is the lead that points to the office

bottom_line.channel_13f: 8,842 active 13F filers; 75% already ADV-reachable. Net-new SFO channel = 13-15 high-confidence name/known-identifiable, plus an estimated 120-220 neutrally-named SFOs hidden in a 1,688 net-new pool requiring per-candidate research. Realistic net-new qualifying yield: 40-90 records.
bottom_line.channel_990pf: 29,676 family foundations nationally, ~82% are 990-PF private foundations, but only ~2.4% (~700) exceed $100M. These are LEADS, not FO entities. Realistic FO-record yield after conversion: 60-175 records, high research cost per lead.
bottom_line.combined_net_new_toward_500: Order-of-magnitude 100-265 net-new qualifying records plausibly sourceable from these two channels combined, heavily verification-effort-bounded; neither channel is a turnkey list. The 13F channel is higher precision but small; the 990-PF channel is larger but lead-quality with low conversion.
bottom_line.caveat: All yield figures are effort-dependent estimates, not counts. Only the raw filing/entity counts (8,842 filers; 892 FTS filings; 29,676 foundations; sample rates) are measured.
